title: Completed-linear affine projections of a morphism of formal modules
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme, I an ideal sheaf, F and H coherent formal modules, alpha a morphism and U an affine open [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Put A=Gamma(U,O_X), R=AdicCompletion(I(U),A) and K=I(U)R [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. There exist finite R-modules M,N, an R-linear map f:M->N, A-linear projections p_n:M|_A->Gamma(U,F_n), and additive projections q_n:N->Gamma(U,H_n). Every p_n is surjective; p_n(x)=0 iff x belongs to K^(n+1)M, and q_n(y)=0 iff y belongs to K^(n+1)N. The maps intertwine f and alpha and p_m=F(l->m)(U) p_l for m<=l.

source.place: Stacks Project Tags 087W and 087X, affine limit construction and calculation of claim (a)

proof.text: Apply the affine section adic-tower theorem to F and H on U, obtaining finite levels, annihilation and the successor quotient equations.

Use completed scalar limits and finite adic-tower limits for both towers. Define p and q by the limit projections. The scalar residue equation and joint injectivity of the limit projections make the map induced by alpha completed-linear.

Transport the A-ideal-power kernel formulas to the extended R-ideal via restrictScalars_map_smul_eq. Limit naturality gives the intertwining and transition equations. This is the explicit Lean calculation in the theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem coherentFormalModule_completed_projections_linear
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (F H : CoherentFormalModule X I) (α : F ⟶ H) (U : X.affineOpens) :
    let A := Γ(X, U.1)
    let R := AdicCompletion (I.ideal U) A
    let J := (I.ideal U).map (algebraMap A R)
    ∃ (M N : ModuleCat.{u} R) (f : M ⟶ N),
      Module.Finite R M ∧ Module.Finite R N ∧
      ∃ (p : ∀ n : ℕ, ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A R)).obj M)
          →ₗ[A] Γ(F.obj.obj (op n), U.1))
        (q : ∀ n : ℕ, N →+ Γ(H.obj.obj (op n), U.1)),
        (∀ n : ℕ, Function.Surjective (p n)) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : M), p n x = 0 ↔
          x ∈ J ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℕ) (y : N), q n y = 0 ↔
          y ∈ J ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule R N)) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : M), q n (f x) = (α.hom.app (op n)).app U.1 (p n x)) ∧
        (∀ (l m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ l) (x : M),
          p m x = (F.obj.map (homOfLE h).op).app U.1 (p l x))
